title: Assembly of Nuna (Columbia)
summary: Nuna, also called Columbia, is described as an early supercontinent that came together in the Paleoproterozoic. One 2024 study puts a first stage of amalgamation at 2.0–1.8 billion years ago and a second stage at 1.8–1.6; a review dates the supercontinent itself to 1.9–1.8 billion years ago.

uncertainty.note: Sources differ: 2.0–1.8 Ga for first-stage amalgamation (Scientific Reports); 1.9–1.8 Ga for the supercontinent (Reddy and Evans). The same study gives a second stage at 1.8–1.6 Ga. No error bars given.

where.modern_name: Greenland (proxy pin only; the assembly involved many cratons and has no single location)

paleo.not_applicable: Predates reliable plate reconstructions; the pin is a proxy and the process is global.

importance.justification: Described as Earth's first supercontinent in one source, marking early global plate-tectonic organisation.

sources.title: Metamorphic turnover at 2 Ga related to two-stage assembly of Columbia
sources.author: Kirscher, Uwe et al.

sources.title: Palaeoproterozoic supercontinents and global evolution: correlations from core to atmosphere
sources.publisher: Yale University, Department of Earth and Planetary Sciences (paper by Reddy and Evans)
sources.author: S. M. Reddy and D. A. D. Evans

reviewer_note: Dates differ between sources (2.0–1.8 vs 1.9–1.8 Ga); pin is a Greenland proxy, not a location. The Yale PDF text has a garbled dash, so the as_recorded entry omits the 1.9.
